title: Investigating individual writing style as a contributor to gender gaps in science and technology
abstract: arXiv:2204.13805v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Gender gaps in how scientific work is evaluated are well documented, but their sources remain debated. We ask whether an overlooked factor---the linguistic style of the writing itself---is gendered and consequential. Drawing on a framework that distinguishes informational features (which emphasize facts) from involved features (which emphasize relationships), we analyze single-authored abstracts of academic papers and patents across all fields of science and technology. Women's writing is systematically more involved than men's---richer in relational, audience-oriented features and higher in the balance of involved to informational language---a difference that holds across scientific fields, in collaborative as well as single-authored work, and in a large open-access biomedical corpus, throughout the full text of papers, not only their abstracts. This stylistic signature also shapes how work is received---papers whose abstracts

translated_title: 探究个人写作风格对科学技术领域性别差距的影响
translated_abstract: 摘要：科学工作评估中的性别差距已有充分记录，但其根源仍存争议。我们探讨一个可能被忽视的因素——写作本身的语言风格——是否具有性别差异并产生影响。基于一个区分信息性特征（强调事实）与参与性特征（强调关系）的框架，我们分析了所有科学技术领域学术论文和专利的单一作者摘要。女性的写作系统性地比男性更具参与性——更富含关系性、面向读者的特征，且参与性语言与信息性语言的平衡比例更高——这种差异在科学领域、合作及单一作者工作中均存在，并在大型开放获取生物医学语料库中贯穿论文全文（不仅限于摘要）得到验证。这种风格特征也影响作品的接受度——摘要具有某种特征的论文……
tldr: 本研究发现女性科学写作更具参与性和关系导向性，这种风格差异普遍存在且影响学术成果的接受度，揭示了写作风格作为性别差距的潜在来源。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that women's scientific writing is more involved and relationship-oriented, a stylistic difference that persists across fields and influences how work is received, highlighting writing style as an overlooked contributor to gender gaps.
